I will keep my land mainly in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the steadiest way for me to make use of the full year, and I trust it more than trying a risky switch. I will plant improved winter wheat first because it sells easily, fits my field habits, and gives me a solid grain crop before summer. After wheat harvest, I will go straight into hybrid summer maize because it has strong yield and matches the local heat and rainfall better than other options. I will keep fertilizer moderate instead of excessive, because inputs are expensive and I want stable returns, not just high spending. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, since wheat in my area usually needs water support, while summer maize can use the rainy season better. I will use rotary tillage for wheat after the summer crop and then lighter field preparation for maize so I can turn the season quickly. I will spray only as needed for common diseases, weeds, and insects, because I want to protect yield but also control cost.
